page.layout: One printed page, one column of running text, with marginal notes in the right margin. Below the text, the last line "Non" stands alone at the right as a catchword.

main_text.p: [?]is aliquid admixtum reperitur, qua quidem appetentiam excitant, ac palato gratificantur, sed magis exiccant, quocirca sanis marini-mi cancri aptiores sunt, nec non iis qui insa-Innaletus dine affe-ctus fluuiatilis amnis cancri salubriores.lubri corporis sunt habitu, vitiosisq; humo-ribus scatent, humorum enim putredini ob-sistunt, superuacuaque excrementa exiccant atque absumunt: fluuiatiles vetò humectant ac nutriunt magis, natiuumque [?]homorem, quo corpus subsistit ac nutritur, adaugent, adhibito vino dulci & calorifico, cuius adiumento concoctio perficitur. Efficacius omnia praestant in aqua hordei loti, inque carnium vel capi iure cocti. Salis quoque & aromatum vsum non incosulto hic adhibent, qui ad aquilonios tractus vergunt, hac enim ratione minus pituitosi efficiuntur, minusq; computrescunt, liquescit enim saliis adeps, vt videre est in limacibus, quae asperso sale, minus sunt opimae ac [?]mostrosè obesæ. Squillæ praeterea aftacos & locustas in eo quod hecticis aeque morbo extenuatis eximiè prosint, vincere reperio, carnisq; dulcedine superare, easdemq; non in vilibus apud Romanos fuisse cibis, Satyrographorum carmina satis testantur, de qua re Iuuenalis,

p.i: Aspice quam in magno distinet pectore lancem,

page.notes: The right-margin notes are printed as separate short lines beside the text; they are transcribed together in the first note above, with line breaks not kept. The first word of the page is a fragment and is marked [?]. "homorem" and "mostrosè" are doubtful readings. The word "Innaletus" and the note "dine affe-ctus" are only partly legible on the scan, so the note reading is reconstructed and uncertain. The verse lines are italic. The final "Non" is the catchword.
